breadth_topics.research_prompt: Independently source affine spaces, affine combinations, affine hull; distinguish convex from affine hull and avoid unstated finite-dimensional assumptions.
Independently source independence of events and of sigma-algebras or random variables, preserving pairwise versus mutual independence.
Independently source trace of finite square matrices over specified rings/fields; distinguish operator trace in finite-dimensional contexts.
Independently source simple-graph cycles/circuits and distinguish paths, walks, directed cycles and graph-theoretic conventions.
Independently source congruence modulo positive integers and modular equivalence; distinguish residue class and representative.
Independently research a separate measure/analysis branch outside recently reviewed concepts; retain source-specific hypotheses.
Independently research a topology or geometry topic with a new contextual meaning, comparing only likely collisions.
Independently research algebraic structures or logic with source-specific scope, avoiding hidden convention shifts.

Functional analysis: independently source normed/Banach-space concepts, continuous linear operators, boundedness and operator norm. Check existing independent meanings and separate norm from induced topology.
Graph theory: source proper vertex coloring and chromatic number in simple undirected graphs, including finite-versus-infinite coloring and the empty graph convention.
Metric and dynamical systems: source contractions, fixed points and iterations with exact domain/codomain and completeness assumptions; distinguish a contraction mapping from the fixed-point theorem.
Differential geometry: source smooth manifolds, smooth charts/atlases and tangent vectors with specified regularity and topological hypotheses.
Algebraic topology: source paths, homotopy of paths and the fundamental group, carefully differentiating based versus unbased homotopies.
Elementary number theory: source gcd, Euler totient, multiplicative function, preserving empty-set and positive-number conventions.
Model theory/logic: source first-order signature, structure, interpretation and satisfaction; separate variables, assignments and sentences.
Numerical analysis: source matrix condition number, spectral radius and convergence of iterative methods without assuming unjustified norms or diagonalisability.
Probability: source stochastic processes, discrete-time Markov chains and transition matrices with explicit state-space, time-homogeneity and row/column conventions.
Convex optimization: source convex functions, convex conjugates, subgradients and strong duality only with exact domain and assumptions; avoid mistaking theorem statements for definitions.
Foundational set theory: source cardinal and ordinal numbers, ordinals as transitive well-ordered sets, successor ordinals and equivalence by bijection.
General topology: source Hausdorff/T1/T0 separation conditions, regularity and normality with explicit space-level T1 conventions.
Enumerative combinatorics: source ordinary and exponential generating functions and formal power series without assuming analytic convergence.
Measure theory: source Carathéodory measurability, measurable maps, almost everywhere and null sets; differentiate completed versus noncompleted measure spaces.
Dynamics: source topological dynamical system, invariant subset, orbit, periodic point and recurrence in discrete time.
